unit.title: Subject Pronouns & Ser: Ustedes vs. Vosotros

lesson.title: Building Sentences with Ser: Identity, Origin, Profession, and Description
lesson.subject: spanish

contentBlocks.text: You've built the pronoun chart, drilled the swaps, and toured the dialects. Today you put ser to work for real, building full sentences in four everyday jobs it does: saying who someone is, where they're from, what they do for work, and what they're like.

Ser handles four big jobs, and you already have every piece you need:

1. Identity — Yo soy Ana. (I am Ana.)
2. Origin — Ella es de Perú. (She is from Perú.)
3. Profession — Nosotros somos maestros. (We are teachers.)
4. Description — Ustedes son mis amigos. (You all are my friends.)

Remember: this course builds every one of these with the Latin American forms only — soy, eres, es, somos, son — using ustedes for 'you all,' never vosotros. The pattern is always pronombre + ser form + the rest of the sentence.

Practice building your own before the activity below:

- (yo / identity) Yo soy... 
- (tú / description) Tú eres... 
- (él or ella / origin) Él es de... / Ella es de... 
- (nosotros / profession) Nosotros somos... 
- (ustedes or ellos / description) Ustedes son... / Ellos son...

Try saying one full sentence out loud for each line before you move on.

You just built real ser sentences across all four of its major jobs — identity, origin, profession, and description — using only the forms this course teaches. Tomorrow: a mini-quiz on the whole week, plus a reflection on choosing the right pronombre for the moment.

objectives: Build correct ser sentences across all four core uses: identity, origin, profession, and description
Use the correct Latin American ser form (soy, eres, es, somos, son) for a given pronombre
materialsNeeded: Device for the build-the-sentence activity (optional — can be done on paper)
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review the four jobs of ser with the child, one example each.
2. Practice the fill-in-the-blank practice set out loud together.
3. Complete the build-the-sentence activity.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's mini-quiz and reflection.
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just identity and origin (soy/es) before adding profession and description
Ready for more: have them write one original sentence per ser job about a real person they know
If word order feels shaky, point out the consistent pattern — pronombre, then the ser form, then the rest — across every example
teacherGuide.answerKey: Yo soy estudiante. Ella es de Perú. Nosotros somos maestros. Ustedes son mis amigos. (Other correct completions of the practice-set sentences are acceptable as long as the ser form matches its pronombre.)
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Delivers Day 4's scope-and-sequence design — sentence-building with ser across identity, origin, profession, and description — as productive practice with the exact Latin American forms this course teaches and tests, directly setting up Friday's mini-quiz.

worksheet.title: Building Sentences with Ser: Identity, Origin, Profession, and Description

generationData.instructions: Complete each sentence with the correct form of ser, then write what job (identity, origin, profession, or description) it does.

rows.problem: Yo ___ (soy/eres/es) de Washington. — ¿Qué trabajo hace ser aquí?
Tú ___ (soy/eres/es) muy inteligente. — ¿Qué trabajo hace ser aquí?
Nosotros ___ (somos/son/es) estudiantes de español. — ¿Qué trabajo hace ser aquí?
Write one original sentence using ustedes + son.
